full_judgment:
2. The respondents 1 and 2 of Civil Appeal No.167 of 2014 Noor Mia and another as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.119 of 1994 against United Engineers and Planters Limited and others for Specific Performance of Contract in respect of the land described in the schedule to the plaint of that suit. On the other hand, appellants Syed Badrul Haque and others filed Title Suit No.09 of 1994 in the Second Court the then Subordinate Judge, Sylhet for declaration of title in respect of .1321 acre of land out of .6080 acre of plot No.7526 khatian No.1255 of Mouza Sylhet Municipality Mohalla Dupadighir Purbapar and for partition. Both the suits were heard analogously and disposed of by a common judgment. The trial Court decreed the suit in Title Suit No.09 of 1994 in preliminary form and allowed saham in favour of the appellant Syed Badrul Haque and others to the extent of the land measuring an area of .1275 acre. It also decreed Title Suit No.119 of 1994. The Defendant United Engineers and Planters Limited and others preferred First Appeal No.161 of 1.999 against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.9 of 1994 and First Appeal No.160 of 1999 against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.119 of 1994. The High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and decree, allowed the First Appeal No.161 of 1999 and dismissed the First Appeal No.160 of 1999. Then the Plaintiff Syed Badul Haque and others preferred C.A. No.353 of 2015 against the First Appeal No.161 of 1999 and the United Engineers and Planters Ltd. preferred Civil Appeal No.167 of 1994 against the judgment and decree of First Appeal No.160 of 1999. 

 3. Plaintiffs" ease in Title Suit No.9 of 1994, in short, was that the land measuring an area of .6080 acre appertaining to khatian No.1255 and plot No.7526 of Mohalla Dhupadighir Purbapar within Mouza Sylhet Municipality, P.S. Kotwali belonged to their sister Syeda Nazira Banu. She died on 12.12.1965 leaving her three consanguine brothers, namely- Syed Sadrul Huq, Syed Badrul Huq, Syed Shafiqul Huq (plaintiff Nos. 1-3), Syed Nazmul Huq and consanguine sisters Hafsa Begum (plaintiff No.4) and Fatema Begum (defendant No.5). Accordingly, the plaintiff Nos.l-3 and Syed Nazmul Huq each inherited .12 acre of land and plaintiff No.4 and defendant no.5 each inherited .06 acre of land. Syed Nazmul Huq died on 19.09.1974 leaving behind his aforesaid 3 full brothers (the plaintiff Nos. 1-3), sisters, the plaintiff No.4 and the defendant No.5 and mother Mobaraka Khatun. On the death of Nazmul Huq his interest to the extent of .12 acre of land was inherited by his mother Mobaraka Khatun to the extent of .02 acre, the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 to the extent of .0250 acre each and sisters, the plaintiff No.4 and the defendant No.5 to the extent' of .0125 acre each. Syeda Mobaraka Khatun died on 13.11.1982 leaving behind aforesaid 3 sons, the plaintiff Nos. 13, 2 daughters, the plaintiff No.4 and the defendant No.5 and 2 grand daughters (son's daughters), the defendant No.3 and defendant No.4. Thus, .02 acre of land left by Syed Mobaraka Khatun was devolved upon the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 who inherited .0040 acre of land each. The plaintiff No and defendant no.5 each got .0020 acre of land while defendant Nos. 3 and 4 acquired .0040 acre of land. Thus, the plaintiffs nos. 1-3 inherited .1490 acre of land, the plaintiff No.4 and defendant No,5 inherited .0745 acre of land and defendant Nos. 3 and 4 jointly inherited 0040 acre of land. Thereafter, the defendant No.5 transferred .07375 acre of land to the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 by a sale deed dated 18.11.1980. Thus, plaintiff Nos. 1-3 acquired .5275 acre of land while the plaintiff No.4 and defendant No.5 acquired .0745 acre of land. Excluding the land sold by defendant No.5 to the plain-tiff Nos.1-3 she had an interest to the extent .0080 acre of land in the suit land. The plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4 transferred .4619 acre of land to the defendant No.1 by 3 kabala deeds. The defendant No.1 was their monthly tenant of the structures standing in the suit land. The suit land was remaining in ejmali. The plaintiffs through plaintiff No.2 approached the Managing Director of the defendant No.1 on 01.01.1994 to get the suit land partitioned claiming their unsold .1321 acre of land but the defendant no.2 denied their title and to effect partition the same. Under the circumstances, the plaintiffs prayed for a preliminary decree in their favour in respect of .1321 acre of land on declaration of their title thereto. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (who are also defendants in Title Suit No.119 of 1994) contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying material allegations contending that suit plot No.7526 measuring an area of .5937 acre which the contesting defendants along with their partners had been possessing as monthly tenants under the plaintiffs by running their business therein. While in such possession, the plaintiff No.1 transferred his interest to the defendant No.1 by a kabala deed dated 12.01.1985. The plaintiff No.2 transferred his interest by another kabala deed dated 31.07.1984 to the defendant No. l. The plaintiff No.4 transferred his share to the defendant No.1 by another kabala deed dated 19.12.1984. Similarly, the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 also transferred their interest by a kabala dated 19.12.1984 to the defendant No. l. By this way, entire area of the land appertaining to suit plot No.7526 was transferred to the defendant No.1 mentioning specific boundaries thereof. By a separate receipt the structures and fixtures standing on the suit land were transferred by the plaintiffs at a consideration of taka 7,70,000/- to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. After purchase, the defendant Nos.1 and 2 got suit plot No.7526 and mutated in their names opening a new khatian being No.1394 within the knowledge of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.3-5. The contesting defendants constructed a community centre in the suit land. The plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. In order to make an illegal gain they instituted Title Suit No.09 of 1994 on false and concocted allegations which was liable to be dismissed.
